sections.heading: Version A and Version B
sections.intro: Version A and Version B can use different answers, so the letter on your paper is the first answer check.
paragraphs: Do not assume that two players in the same classroom received the same sheet. If a friend calls out a choice, compare versions before changing anything. A correct letter for Version B can be wrong for the same question number on Version A.

The Phone route avoids most version confusion because it processes your own photographed sheet. Saved answer fragments are still useful as examples of how numbered corrections look, but they should not replace the current paper.

sections.heading: The All-A + Phone Method
sections.intro: The All-A baseline shortens the Phone workload because answers already correct as A can be skipped.
paragraphs: Fill the sheet carefully from the first question to the last. The goal is not to submit all A; it is to give every row a baseline so the Phone can return only the non-A corrections.
After the scan, leave skipped rows at A. If the Phone shows a pair such as question 2 with D, go to row 2 and change only that bubble. Continue until the Phone has processed the whole sheet.

sections.heading: How to Correct the Questions the Phone Returns
sections.intro: Question numbers matter more than memorizing a sequence of letters.
paragraphs: Read every result as a pair: number first, letter second. Apply small batches in ascending order, then recount the row before moving on. If the Phone jumps from question 2 to question 5, leave questions 3 and 4 alone unless a later batch names them.

A common low-score mistake is shifting every later correction up one row after a skipped number. Another is stopping after the first Phone batch when more corrections remain. Use another safe window if the device has not reached the end of the sheet.

hero.heading: How Not to Get Caught in Cheating During Testing
hero.lead: Watch the teacher before every gadget action, prepare the sheet while the Phone is hidden, use short scan windows, put the device away early and account for Anxiety and Snitches before pushing for another correction.

sections.heading: How Not to Get Caught in Cheating During Testing
sections.intro: Make the exposed part of the answer loop as short as possible.

steps.heading: Prepare first
steps.description: Check Version A/B and fill the All-A baseline before pulling out the Phone.

steps.heading: Observe the teacher

steps.heading: Repeat only when safe
steps.description: Use another opening for the next batch rather than overstaying one window.

sections.heading: Watch the Teacher Before Taking a Risk
paragraphs: Look once, decide and act. Repeatedly turning the camera without moving the paper forward wastes time and can make the situation harder to read.
When the teacher changes direction, treat the opening as finished. The exact sight radius and timing can change during BETA, so use visible attention rather than a fixed number of seconds.

sections.heading: How Anxiety Fits Into a Test
paragraphs: Anxiety adds pressure while you manage the paper and classroom. Return focus to the desk between observations, keep the pencil work moving and avoid long exposed gadget sessions.
If the current Anxiety cues intensify, simplify the next action. Finish a visible correction, hide the Phone and recover the test rhythm before scanning again.

sections.heading: How Snitches Affect Risk
paragraphs: Snitches can expose players for Credits, so teacher direction is not the only thing to watch. A classmate who keeps looking toward your desk can turn a safe-looking Phone window into social risk.
Coordinate only with friends you trust, compare Version A/B before sharing answers and avoid displaying the Phone longer than the correction requires.

links.label: Snitching guide
links.description: Understand the reporting mechanic and its current in-game prompts.

sections.heading: When to Put the Phone Away
paragraphs: Hide the Phone when the teacher turns, another player starts watching, Anxiety becomes difficult to manage or the timer threatens submission. Do not wait for a final warning if the room has already changed.
The All-A method helps because it shortens the correction list. Use that time saving to end the window earlier, not to keep the device visible for more optional actions.

sections.heading: A Safer Scan-and-Correct Routine
paragraphs: Use a repeatable rhythm: baseline while hidden, teacher check, short scan, hide, numbered corrections, desk reset and another check. Each step can stop safely when the room changes.
Once this rhythm consistently finishes tests, improve speed one part at a time. A faster route should reduce exposed seconds without sacrificing row alignment or final review.

faq.question: How do I avoid getting caught in Cheating During Testing?
faq.answer: Prepare the sheet first, watch the teacher, use short Phone windows and hide as soon as attention changes.

faq.question: How long is a safe Phone window?
faq.answer: Use the current teacher direction rather than a fixed number of seconds, because BETA behavior can change.

faq.question: What should I do when Anxiety rises?
faq.answer: Return focus to the desk, hide the Phone and resume with a smaller action after the test rhythm settles.

faq.question: Can Snitches get you caught?
faq.answer: Yes. Keep gadget use brief and cooperate only with players you trust.

faq.question: Should I risk one more answer for 100%?
faq.answer: Not when the teacher or timer threatens the run. A strong submitted paper is better than an unfinished or caught perfect attempt.
